summary: Iteration 2 frontend testing of Redactorium's 4 new features (Custom Regex Rules, Sample Match Drill-Down, Bundled ZIP Download, DOCX round-trip infra). 13/13 checks passed with zero console errors. Custom rules panel expands/collapses, validates regex (invalid rejected via toast), tests match/no-match live, saves+persists via localStorage across reload, and deletes correctly. Uploading a CSV with X##### values yielded 'Custom-ID' as top detector on the customid column with 85% confidence and a purple 'custom' pill. Drill-down toggle reveals a drill-panel-<i> row with exactly 3 example pill chips using real column values; link text toggles 'show 3 examples' <-> 'hide examples'. After applying sample data, download-zip-btn triggers a browser download matching /redactorium-evidence-\d+\.zip/. Regression: existing three individual download buttons still emit the same filenames (sample-contacts.redacted.csv, redactorium-log.json, redactorium-record.pdf). App compiles/loads cleanly which indirectly confirms docxHandler import is fine. Real .docx round-trip through the UI was not exercised (would require constructing a valid DOCX in-browser); flagged as deferred, not a regression.
critical_code_review_comments: customRules.js compileRule: test() returns rule.base ?? 0.85 while the confidence path in detector likely re-adds columnHintBoost; verify no double-scoring above 1.0 (not observed in tests).
CustomRulesPanel uses Math.random-based id; two rules created in same tick could theoretically collide (very low risk).
DOCX real round-trip not verified end-to-end; a small in-browser JSZip fixture in future tests would close this gap.
seed_data_creation: Ephemeral CSV (X12345/X67890/X99999) uploaded in-browser; localStorage custom rule cleared at test end via delete flow.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All new iteration-2 features work. If future iteration touches DOCX, add a JSZip-based in-browser DOCX generator and drive it through file-input to fully verify docxHandler round-trip and mime-type in the download.
